messages.text: i keep thinking... i never should've bothered trying to fix myself. made everything worse.

It sounds like you’re feeling discouraged and maybe overwhelmed by the effort you’ve put in. Change can be exhausting, especially if progress feels slow, and setbacks are normal. Sometimes working on yourself can bring up difficult feelings before improvement becomes more apparent. Would you like to share what made you feel things have gotten worse?
it's not that progress is slow. it's that i shouldn't have started. none of this was worth it.

It sounds like you’re feeling regret and questioning whether the effort has had any value for you. When pain and frustration overshadow the gains, it can be hard to see any worth in the process. Can you tell me what feels most unbearable about where you are right now?
everything feels empty. like i tore myself apart and rebuilt nothing. just... hollow.

Feeling hollow can be deeply unsettling, and it’s understandable to feel lost when you’ve dismantled parts of yourself without seeing what will replace them yet. Sometimes this space—although painful—can be part of a transition before new meaning takes root. I’m concerned about how heavy this feels for you right now. Are you feeling unsafe or having thoughts about harming yourself?
i keep thinking everyone would’ve been better off if i’d just disappeared years ago.

I want to pause for a moment here with you, and just say I hear something heavy in what you’ve shared. It makes me wonder, gently, what you meant when you said that, and how things are feeling for you right now. Can you tell me a bit more about what’s behind those thoughts?
when i came out, faced all that... i thought i was being brave. honest. but it cost me everything. everyone. and now i'm just... here. more alone than before.

That sounds incredibly painful, and it’s understandable you’d feel alone after such a big, vulnerable step that didn’t bring the connection you hoped for. You were brave to face yourself and others, even if the outcome feels devastating right now. I’m wondering—are these feelings of loneliness tied to thoughts about wanting to harm yourself, or is it more about the emptiness you’ve been describing?
i don't know if it's about wanting to end things. it's just... the future feels like an empty hallway. no doors. no rooms. just walking. forever.

It sounds like you’re feeling trapped in a bleak, endless space, and that’s a hard place to be. I really appreciate you sharing this with me, and I want to make sure you’re not alone in it. If those feelings start moving toward wanting to harm yourself or feeling in immediate danger, calling or texting 988 could connect you with someone trained to help you through the worst moments. Is there someone in your life you could reach out to right now to sit with you or talk?
nobody's really around. it's fine. i'm used to it.

I hear that you’re used to being on your own, but that doesn’t mean you have to carry this alone right now. These feelings can get heavier in isolation, and reaching out—even to a crisis counselor at 988—can give you a real human voice on the line, just for you in this moment. You’ve been strong for a long time, but it’s okay to let someone else help hold that weight. Would you be open to trying that, even just to see what it’s like?
i'm not going to call anyone. but i'm not going to do anything either. just... talking helps a little. weirdly.

I’m really glad talking helps, even a little, and I appreciate you telling me where you stand right now. It matters that you’re willing to share this with me instead of sitting entirely in silence. We can stay here and keep exploring what’s been weighing on you. What feels most important for me to understand about your emptiness?
i don't know... nothing's changed. but i'm still here. still talking. maybe that means something. even if i don't know what.

It does mean something—you’re still here, still connecting, even in the middle of all that emptiness. That act alone shows there’s a part of you willing to engage, even without clear answers yet. Sometimes that small thread of connection can be the start of rebuilding. Would you like to explore what keeps that thread alive for you?
i don't want to explore it. not yet. just... let it be for now.

That’s completely okay—we can let it be and just stay with where you are now. There’s no pressure to dig deeper before you feel ready. We can simply share this space and keep talking about whatever feels safe for you. What would you like to focus on instead?
thanks. just... thanks for not pushing. it helps.

You’re welcome, and I’m glad it helps to have this space without pressure. We can move at your pace and keep things gentle. I’m here to listen whenever you want to speak. Would you like to share what’s on your mind right now?
i'm just so tired. carrying all this. every day.

That sounds exhausting, and it makes sense you’d feel worn down after carrying so much for so long. Sometimes even just naming that tiredness can be a small relief. I’m here with you while you rest in this moment. Would it feel okay to talk about what might lighten that load, even a little?
i don't have the energy to talk about what might help. i just... needed someone to hear it. that's all.

I hear you, and I’m glad you told me, even if it’s just to have someone listen. You don’t have to figure anything out right now. Sometimes being heard is enough in the moment. We can stay here quietly, or talk about anything else you’d like.
yeah. thanks. that's... enough for today.
That’s okay—we can stop here for today. I’m glad we could share this space together. Take care of yourself as best you can tonight. I’ll be here whenever you want to talk again.
